item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Multi-line call history tabs in the Calls app
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Teams is introducing a redesigned call history experience for Teams Phone users who have multi-line calling enabled. Call activity, including call history, voicemails, and recordings, will be organized by phone line in dedicated tabs within the Calls app.

This change simplifies navigation for users who manage multiple phone lines.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete by early October 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Teams Phone users with multi-line calling enabled and multiple phone numbers assigned
  • Users without multi-line calling enabled are not affected

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams desktop for Windows
  • Microsoft Teams desktop for Mac
  • Microsoft Teams on the web
  • Teams Phone

What will happen

  • A dedicated tab will be created in the Calls app for each assigned phone line.
  • Call history will be displayed under the phone line associated with the activity.
  • Voicemails will appear under the phone line where they were received.
  • Call recordings will appear under the phone line associated with the call.
  • Users will be able to view and manage activity separately for each phone line.
  • The feature will be enabled automatically for eligible users with multi-line calling configured.
  • No changes will occur for users who do not use multi-line calling.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required.

We recommend that you:

  • Notify your help desk and support teams about the updated Calls app experience.
  • Inform affected users who manage multiple phone lines.
  • Update internal documentation, training materials, and support content that references call history, voicemail, or recordings in the Teams Calls app.

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Hide organizer names in calendar view on Teams Panels
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft Teams Panels will introduce a new administrator setting that allows administrators to choose whether organizer names are shown in Calendar View on Teams Panels.

Admins can toggle the Show organizer name setting ON or OFF in the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal or on the panel device. When organizer names are hidden, the organizer name is not shown in Calendar View on the panel device.

This feature is available with Teams Rooms Pro and Teams Shared Spaces licenses.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning in early October 2026 and expected to complete by early October 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Administrators who manage Microsoft Teams Panels
  • Organizations using Teams Rooms Pro licenses
  • Organizations using Teams Shared Spaces licenses
  • Users who view meeting information on Teams panel devices

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams Panels
  • Teams Rooms Pro Management portal

What will happen

  • A new setting, Show organizer name, will be available for Teams panel devices.
  • Administrators can choose whether organizer names are displayed in Calendar View.
  • The setting can be configured from the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal or directly on a Teams panel device.
  • By default, organizer names will continue to be displayed in Calendar View.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required if you want organizer names to continue appearing in Calendar View on Teams panel devices.

If you want to hide organizer names:

  • Review your room privacy and display requirements.
  • Update the Show organizer name setting in the Teams Rooms Pro Management portal or on individual Teams panel devices.

Learn more

  • Release notes for devices in Microsoft Teams - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Administrators can enable or disable the display of organizer names on Teams Panels. The available information does not indicate support for management through Entra ID group membership.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Copilot: Introducing the Microsoft plugin registry for Microsoft Copilot experiences
item.description:
[What and why]

We are introducing the Microsoft plugin registry to Microsoft Copilot experiences. The Microsoft plugin registry provides a shared catalog for discovering, publishing, and governing organization-approved and custom-built plugins across Microsoft Copilot experiences (Chat, Cowork, Code, Autopilot) and Microsoft 365 apps (Word, PowerPoint, Excel) and SharePoint. Plugins can bundle agents, skills, connectors, and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers into a single package that can be published, discovered, governed, and acquired through the Microsoft 365 admin center and Microsoft Agent 365.

As part of this update, the Agents, Agents & Skills, and Customize buttons will be replaced by a new Plugins button. This change reduces the need to repeat discovery and setup processes by providing users with a more consistent way to discover and access approved plugins across supported Copilot experiences. Admins will continue to manage agents in the Agents settings within the Microsoft 365 admin center and Microsoft Agent 365.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): This change consists of two rollouts:
    1. Plugin registry: Rollout began in late September 2026 and is expected to complete by late October 2026.
    2. User interface changes: Rollout begins in late October 2026 and is expected to complete by late November 2026.

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft 365 admins who manage plugins and users who access agents, skills, connectors, or MCP servers through supported Microsoft Copilot experiences.

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Copilot Chat
  • Microsoft Copilot Cowork
  • Microsoft Copilot Code
  • Microsoft Copilot Autopilot
  • Microsoft Word
  • Microsoft PowerPoint
  • Microsoft Excel
  • Microsoft SharePoint
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft Agent 365

What will happen

  • Microsoft 365 admins will be able to discover, publish, govern, and manage plugins centrally under Tools in the Microsoft 365 admin center and Microsoft Agent 365.
  • Users will be able to access approved plugins through a more consistent experience, reducing the need to repeat discovery and setup processes across supported Copilot experiences.
  • By late November 2026, users will select Plugins instead of Agents, Agents & Skills, or Customize to find agents.

Updated Tools menu in the Microsoft 365 admin center

[Action required and recommendations]

No action or setup is required to enable this change, and no technical migration is required. We recommend that you:

  • Update internal documentation, training, and adoption materials that reference Agents, Agents & Skills, or Customize.
  • Prepare users for the Agents, Agents & Skills, and Customize buttons to be replaced by the new Plugins button.
  • Review which plugin capabilities should be available to users based on your organization’s governance requirements.

[Learn more]

  • Extend Microsoft 365 Copilot | Microsoft Learn
  • Manage plugins, skills, and MCP servers in Microsoft 365 admin center - Microsoft 365 admin | Microsoft Learn
  • Agent settings in Microsoft 365 admin center - Microsoft 365 admin | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

No compliance considerations identified. Review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Updated Copilot in Microsoft Edge Experience
item.description:

Review the linked documentation or admin center controls for group-based configuration support.

item.title: [planForChange] Action Required: Upgrade ExchangeOnlineManagement PowerShell Module to Version 3.10.1 or Later
item.description:
[What and Why:]

Microsoft introduced security enhancements to Exchange Online PowerShell authentication in ExchangeOnlineManagement module version 3.10.1. These enhancements strengthen the authentication flow and provide protection against emerging threats. Customers using a version earlier than 3.10.1 should upgrade to version 3.10.1 or later. Customers already using version 3.10.1 or later do not need to take additional action beyond keeping the module up to date.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Enforcement of strict logon requirements is scheduled to begin on March 31, 2027.
  • The rollout is scheduled to begin in late March 2027 and be completed by late April 2027.

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

Customers using ExchangeOnlineManagement module versions earlier than 3.10.1

What will happen:

  • ExchangeOnlineManagement versions earlier than 3.10.1 may experience authentication failures in certain interactive authentication scenarios after enforcement begins.
  • The scenario is particularly relevant when PowerShell 7 is used with Web Account Manager (WAM) disabled.
  • You may not be affected if you are using:
    • ExchangeOnlineManagement version 3.10.1 or later
    • Certificate-based authentication
    • WAM-based authentication
    • Windows PowerShell 5.x

[Action Required/Recommendations:]

  1. Identify systems running ExchangeOnlineManagement versions earlier than 3.10.1.
  2. Upgrade affected installations to version 3.10.1 or later before enforcement begins.
  3. Validate administrative scripts, automation solutions, and operational procedures before enforcement.

You can verify installed module versions by running:

Get-Module ExchangeOnlineManagement -ListAvailable

Review the ExchangeOnlineManagement module information and available versions in the PowerShell Gallery.

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft PowerPoint: Temporary removal of the Brand pane

The Brand pane was introduced to provide users with a dedicated place in PowerPoint to discover and use assets from available Brand Kits, including brand colors, logos, images, icons, and fonts. Based on customer feedback, we are refining the experience before making it broadly available. This work will help ensure the feature better meets customer expectations when it returns in a future release.

What will happen

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft OneNote: Multimodal recording in Copilot Notebooks on Windows
item.description:
Updated September 30, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We are introducing multimodal capture in Copilot Notebooks on Windows. This feature enables users to capture audio, images, and notes in a single experience and use Microsoft 365 Copilot to generate structured insights such as summaries, decisions, and action items. This helps users turn meetings, conversations, and offline work into actionable outputs within Copilot Notebooks.

This message is associated with Microsoft 365 Roadmap ID 566322.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Beginning end of October 2026 (previously late September) and expected to complete end of October 2026 (previously mid-October) 

[Impact on Your Organization]

Who is affected

  • Users with access to Copilot Notebooks in OneNote
  • Requires a Microsoft 365 Copilot license
  • Available to commercial Microsoft 365 users with work or school (Entra ID) accounts
  • Users must have the Microsoft 365 desktop apps installed on Windows (including OneNote)

Platforms/Services

  • OneNote (desktop app on Windows)
  • Copilot Notebooks
  • Microsoft 365 Copilot

What will happen

  • Users can capture audio, images, and notes directly into Copilot Notebooks.
  • Capture can be suggested or initiated when supported browser-based meetings are detected (Zoom, Webex, Google Meet).
  • Users can also manually start capture from the OneNote system tray icon.
  • Copilot generates a structured Copilot Page with insights, decisions, and action items based on captured content.
  • Captured content is saved to the selected Copilot Notebook and is available across endpoints.
  • The feature is available by default for eligible users.

[Action Required or Recommendations]

No action is required.

Admins can disable this feature using a policy setting.

  • Review available policy settings if you want to disable the feature.
  • Inform users about organizational policies related to transcription and consent.
  • Organizations should ensure users follow applicable consent and recording policies before capturing or transcribing conversations.

Learn more: 

  • Data, Privacy, and Security for Microsoft 365 Copilot | Microsoft 365 Copilot | Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn
  • Security for Microsoft 365 Copilot | Microsoft 365 Copilot | Microsoft 365 | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change store new customer data?Yes. Captured audio, images, and notes are stored in the user’s selected Copilot Notebook (SharePoint or OneDrive).
Does the change alter how customer data is processed?Yes. Content is transcribed and processed by Microsoft 365 Copilot to generate structured insights.
Does the change introduce AI capabilities interacting with data?Yes. Copilot analyzes captured content to generate summaries, decisions, and action items.
Does the change provide new interaction with generative AI?Yes. Users interact with Copilot-generated outputs based on captured multimodal data.
Does the change add a third party integration?Yes. Supports capture from browser-based meetings including Zoom, Webex, and Google Meet.
Does the change include admin control?Yes. Admins can disable the feature using a policy setting.

item.title: [planForChange] Microsoft Copilot: GPT 6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 beginning to roll out today
item.description:
[What and Why:]

To give users more choice and flexibility when working with AI in Microsoft Copilot, we're expanding the set of AI models available in Microsoft Copilot.

Starting today, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 begin rolling out today with usage-based billing in Cowork and Microsoft Copilot Studio.

GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 will also begin rolling out in phases across Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Chat in the coming week as part of the Microsoft 365 Copilot user subscription license (USL). Limits apply to these models, but they are designed to support broad day-to-day AI usage across organizations and are implemented in such a way that the vast majority of users are not expected to reach them. Users approaching a limit will receive in-product notifications and can continue their work by switching to Auto mode or selecting another available model. 

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability:
  • Cowork and Copilot Studio: Rollout begins today, September 30, 2026.
  • Word, Excel, PowerPoint and Chat: Phased rollout begins in the coming week. 

[Impact on Your Organization:

Who is affected:

  • Cowork and Copilot Studio: Users assigned a user subscription license (USL) with usage-based billing (UBB) enabled.
  • Word, Excel, PowerPoint, and Chat: Users assigned a user subscription license (USL).
  • Access to Claude Sonnet 5.5 additionally requires the Anthropic subprocessor to be enabled in your organization.
  • Access to GPT-6.1 Sol additionally requires the OpenAI subprocessor to be enabled in your organization for select surfaces.

Platforms/Services:

  • (USL) Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat
  • (USL) Microsoft Word
  • (USL) Microsoft Excel
  • (USL) Microsoft PowerPoint
  • (UBB) Copilot Cowork
  • (UBB) Microsoft Copilot Studio

What will happen:

  • Users will be able to select GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 using the model selector from supported Microsoft Copilot experiences.
  • The feature is enabled by default for eligible licensed users who meet the applicable configuration requirements.

[Action Required / Recommendations:]

No action is required for organizations that want users to access these models.

Recommended actions:

  • Review whether the Anthropic subprocessor is enabled if you plan to make Claude Sonnet 5.5 available to users.
  • Review whether the OpenAI subprocessor is enabled if you plan to make GPT-6.1 Sol broadly available to users. If disabled, GPT-6.1 Sol may not be available from all supported Copilot surfaces.
  • Review your organization's AI usage guidance and communicate model availability to end users.
  • Inform helpdesk and support teams that users may encounter usage-limit notifications and can continue working using Auto mode or another available model.
  • Review the announcement blog for additional details: Available today: OpenAI's GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 in Microsoft Copilot | Microsoft Community Hub.
  • Update internal user documentation and training materials, as appropriate.

[Compliance Considerations:]

Consideration Explanation 
Does the change introduce or significantly modify AI/ML or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data? GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5 are additional AI models that users can select within Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences to generate responses based on content and context available to the user through Copilot. 
Does the change provide end users any new way of interacting with generative AI? Users gain access to new model choices, GPT-6.1 Sol and Claude Sonnet 5.5, in supported Microsoft 365 Copilot experiences. 
Does the change include an admin control and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership? Access to Claude Sonnet 5.5 depends on administrative configuration of the Anthropic subprocessor.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Viva Engage: Email updates for frontline users without an active Exchange mailbox
item.description:
Updated September 30, 2026: We have updated the content timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[Introduction]

Viva Engage will stop sending email notifications to users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination. Previously, email notifications could still be attempted for these users, resulting in repeated delivery retries, increased load on email systems, and, in some cases, delays to important business communications.

This change reduces unnecessary email traffic, improves delivery efficiency, and helps ensure important communications are delivered reliably and on time.

Users with supported mailbox configurations, including cloud mailboxes, on-premises mailboxes, shared mailboxes, and other routable email destinations, will continue to receive Viva Engage email notifications as expected.

Notifications delivered through supported channels such as Microsoft Teams remain unaffected.

[When this will happen:]

General Availability (Worldwide): Rollout begins mid-October 2026 (previously end of September) and is expected to complete by end of December 2026 (previously end of October).

[How this affects your organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Microsoft 365 admins managing Viva Engage users and mailbox configurations.

What will happen:

  • Viva Engage will no longer attempt to send email notifications to users who do not have a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Users with cloud, on-premises, shared, or other supported mailbox configurations will continue to receive email notifications as expected.
  • This change does not affect the existing email notification experience for users with a valid mailbox or routable email destination.
  • Notifications delivered through Microsoft Teams or other supported channels are not impacted.
  • The change is enabled by default and applies automatically.
  • Organizations may see:
    • Reduced load on email systems and gateways.
    • Fewer retry attempts for undeliverable messages.
    • Improved email delivery efficiency and reliability.

[What you can do to prepare:]

  • No action is required.
  • Review your Exchange Online licensing configuration to identify users without mailbox access.
  • Evaluate your notification strategy (e.g., Teams vs. Email) for frontline workers.
  • Inform helpdesk and user support teams of the expected behavior change.
  • Update internal documentation if email notifications are referenced for frontline users.

[Compliance considerations:]

  • Alters how existing customer data is processed: Email notifications to users without mailboxes are no longer attempted, reducing unnecessary processing of undeliverable messages.
  • No other compliance impacts identified.

item.title: [planForChange] Dynamics 365 and Power Platform– Information about storage validation for Dataverse-only tenants
item.description:
Beginning November 9, 2026, we are introducing staged storage validation for supported Dynamics 365 applications. The change gives administrators clearer visibility into storage use, advance notice of potential restrictions, and several ways to remain within capacity, including removing unneeded data, adding capacity, or enabling pay-as-you-go for sandbox environments.

When a tenant exceeds its entitled Database, File, or Log capacity, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations will be restricted immediately. If the overage remains unresolved, sandbox environments that do not have pay-as-you-go billing enabled will enter Administration mode after 30 days of remaining over capacity, allowing access only to administrators. After 60 days, those sandbox environments will be disabled, preventing access for all users. Production environments are not subject to these restrictions and will remain accessible. However, environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations will still be blocked while the tenant remains over capacity.

Deployment Timeline:
  • Rollout begins: November 9, 2026
  • Rollout completion: December 4, 2026
How does this affect me?
The Dataverse storage validation applies only to Dataverse-only tenants without Dynamics 365 Finance and Operations environment(s) or consumption. The products in-scope of storage validation include:
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Sales
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Field Service
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Insights
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Customer Voice
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Contact Center
  • Microsoft Dynamics 365 Project Operations (Dataverse deployments)
If your tenant exceeds its entitled storage capacity, the following lifecycle applies:

Stage Timing Impact
1. Restricted When the tenant first exceeds its entitled storage capacity, known as time zero (T0) Environment creation, copy, restore, and recover operations are blocked
2. Administration mode 30 days after the tenant first exceeds capacity - T0 Only administrators can sign in to *affected sandbox environments. All other users are blocked from accessing the environment.
3. Disabled After 60 unresolved days from T0 All users, including administrators, are blocked from *affected sandbox environments; the environment data is retained and remains available for recovery after remediation

Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing do not progress through the storage overage lifecycle. Other *affected sandbox environments in the tenant may still be affected with restrictions.

We will provide notifications that include the tenant's current storage status, the date it first exceeded capacity, its current lifecycle stage, upcoming restrictions, and recommended remediation actions.

Restrictions are removed after the tenant has returned below 100% of its entitled storage capacity. Sandbox environments with active pay-as-you-go billing are excluded from the lifecycle even if the tenant remains over storage capacity. Processing time may vary depending on the remediation method used.

What action do I need to take?
Review your environment(s) and perform the following actions before November 9, 2026:

item.description:
We are announcing the ability to let customer service representatives set their next presence to handle routing of work items in Dynamics 365 Contact Center. This feature will reach general availability on October 30, 2026.

After all active conversations and work items are completed, the system automatically updates the presence to the selected status. This setting allows customer service representatives to transition smoothly to breaks or other availability states without interrupting customer engagements or requiring manual status changes.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Microsoft Teams: Improved file sharing experience in external chats
item.description:
Updated September 29, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why]

We’re improving the file-sharing experience in Microsoft Teams external (federated) chats by making the Attach file (paperclip) and drag-and-drop experiences available by default. Existing OneDrive, SharePoint, and security controls continue to govern access. This update does not change your OneDrive or SharePoint external-sharing settings or override existing access restrictions.

For files uploaded through these experiences, Teams assigns permissions to chat participants for uploaded files. Senders can still review, modify, or remove file access before sending the message. This reduces the need to assign permissions manually, while allowing senders to stay in control. 

  • More info: Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn
  • Users can already paste file links into external chats; this update makes attaching and sharing files easier within the policies your organization allows.
  • Admins can separately control the Teams attachment experience and automatic permission assignment using Teams PowerShell, as described below. 

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC, GCC High, DoD): Beginning in late October 2026 and expected to complete by late November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Organizations using Microsoft Teams external access (federation)
  • Organizations that previously disabled in external chats
  • Users participating in external 1:1 chats, external group chats, and meeting chats

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • External (federated) 1:1 chats
  • External (federated) group chats
  • Meeting chats
  • Teams desktop app
  • Teams web app

What will happen

  • The ability for users to attach and share files in external chats will be enabled for all Microsoft 365 tenants.
  • Users can already paste file links into external chants. This ability is unchanged. With this change, users will also have the ability to attach files (paperclip) option in external (federated) chats.
  • This change applies even if your organization previously configured this Teams setting as Disabled.
  • Organizations that want the Teams attachment experience in external chats to remain disabled must reapply the disabled setting after rollout.
  • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams assigns permissions to participants in the external chat for files uploaded using Attach or drag-and-drop, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies.
  • Senders can review, modify, or remove sharing permissions before sending a file.
  • Senders can continue to modify or revoke access after a file has been shared.
  • Automatic permission assignment applies only to files uploaded through the attach or drag-and-drop experience.
  • Files uploaded to external chats are stored in the sender's OneDrive and display an External label.
  • Existing OneDrive and SharePoint sharing controls continue to govern access.
  • Existing sensitivity labels, domain restrictions, and security protections continue to apply.
  • Disabling the Teams attachment experience does not prevent users from pasting file links; recipient access remains governed by the file’s permissions and applicable sharing policies.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required to preserve external-sharing restrictions already configured in OneDrive and SharePoint; this update does not change those restrictions. To review or change these controls, see Manage sharing settings for SharePoint and OneDrive in Microsoft 365. 

[To disable file attachments in external chats]

After rollout reaches your tenant, apply the following Teams PowerShell setting:

Set-CsTeamsFilesPolicy -Identity Global -FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers Disabled

Verify the setting:

Get-CsTeamsFilesPolicy | Select Identity, FileSharingInChatsWithExternalUsers

Recommended actions:

  • Review your SharePoint, OneDrive, and Microsoft Entra external sharing configuration because these settings continue to govern what external recipients can access.
  • Inform helpdesk and support teams about the updated attachment experience and the distinction between Teams attachment controls and OneDrive/SharePoint access controls. 
  • Update user training and internal documentation as needed.
  • Communicate to users that:
    • They can attach files directly in chats with people outside the organization.
    • When automatic permission assignment is enabled, Teams grants chat participants access to uploaded files before the message is sent, subject to existing OneDrive and SharePoint policies. Senders can review, modify, or remove access before sending.
    • Pasted file links retain their existing permissions.
    • Files uploaded to external chats are stored in the sender's OneDrive and display an External label.

Optional configuration to allow attachments without automatic permission assignment:

To disable automatic permission assignment while continuing to allow file attachments in external chats:

Set-CsTeamsMessagingPolicy -Identity Global -AutoShareFilesInExternalChats Disabled

If automatic permission assignment is disabled, users may need to manually grant access to shared files before external recipients can open them.

Allow several hours for policy changes to propagate before users see the updated experience.

Learn more:

  • Share files and Loop in external chats - Microsoft Teams | Microsoft Learn

[Compliance considerations]

QuestionAnswer
Does the change alter how existing customer data is processed, stored, or accessed?Yes. Uploaded files shared through Attach or drag-and-drop can automatically receive permissions for participants in external chats. Existing OneDrive and SharePoint controls continue to govern access. Uploaded files are stored in the sender’s OneDrive.
Does the change provide a new way of communicating between users, tenants, or subscriptions?Yes. The direct file-attachment experience in external (federated) chats becomes available by default; the existing ability to paste file links remains unchanged.
Does the change include an admin control, and can it be controlled through Entra ID group membership?Yes. Admins can separately control Teams file attachments and automatic permission assignment through Teams PowerShell policies. OneDrive and SharePoint sharing settings continue to govern external file access.

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Enhanced security and access controls for Outlook attachments
item.description:
Updated September 29, 2026: We have updated the content. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and why:]

As part of our overall security initiatives, we’ve created a separate internal application configuration for Outlook attachments, therefore, all standard security and authentication flows will be handled separately. Moreover, Conditional Access policies are now enforced for Outlook attachment operations. Users who don’t meet company policies won’t be able to download, preview, or upload classic attachments (this includes inline images). Policies assigned to Exchange and Office cloud applications will be inherited by the attachment application by default. Continuous Access Evaluation is not included in the initial rollout but will follow up soon.

Scope: This change is only applicable to Outlook web (OWA) and New Outlook.

[Rollout schedule:]

Available now.

[Impact on your organization:]

  • Your existing policies now cover attachments. Conditional Access policies you have already scoped to Exchange and Office cloud applications will be enforced for attachment scenarios as well. No new policies need to be created.
  • Users out of compliance will be blocked from attachments. If a user's session no longer satisfies a Conditional Access policy — for example, a non-compliant device, a blocked location, or a network change that triggers CAE re-evaluation — attachment operations will be blocked.
  • These are separate follow-up changes we expect to land in the upcoming weeks. We’ll keep you updated on the readiness and rollout of these enhancements:
    • User sign in prompt for remediation. We're currently working on a solution to prompt the user for sign in to recover functionalities when possible. This will depend on the policy configuration; if the user is not compliant, they won’t be able to use attachment-related tasks. We’ll provide an update to customers once we start rolling out this enhancement.
    • Enable Continuous Access Evaluation (CAE). CAE isn’t supported for this new application configuration yet. We’ll update this message with additional content when it becomes available.  

[Action required / Recommendations:]

  1. Review how your Office and Exchange policies apply to attachments.
    1. Attachment operations are now handled by their own application, which by default inherits the Conditional Access policies you've assigned to Office and Exchange. Confirm those conditions are what you intend to enforce for attachments.
    2. If you’ve intentionally excluded Exchange online from a policy, that exclusion doesn't carry over to attachments, so users in scope can reach their mail but will be blocked from downloading, previewing, or uploading attachments.
    3. To manage attachment policies separate from mail, you can either exclude the attachment application from a policy or target it in a policy of its own. Both require a one-time setup step in your tenant — see Appendix: Excluding attachments from a policy.
  2. Update your help desk documentation. Support staff should know that attachment access failures may now result from a Conditional Access policy, and that the remediation is the same as for Outlook — return to a compliant device or network and re-authenticate.
  3. Notify users if you enforce strict Conditional Access policies, so they understand attachment actions may now be blocked under the same conditions that already block access to their mailbox.

[Appendix:]

Excluding attachments from a policy

Attachment operations are handled by an application named OwaDownloadAttachments (application Id: e4f2bb2d-a4d0-4eab-aac6-a8b83471cf64 ). Before you can exclude it from a Conditional Access policy, a service principal for it must exist in your tenant. This is a one-time step you'll need to complete first.

Step 1: Create the service principal

You'll need the Cloud Application Administrator or Global Administrator role.

  1. Open Graph Explorer and sign in as an administrator of your tenant.
  2. Run:

POST https://graph.microsoft.com/v1.0/servicePrincipals

Request body: { "appId": "e4f2bb2d-a4d0-4eab-aac6-a8b83471cf64" }

Consent to Application.ReadWrite.All scope is required.

A successful request returns 201 Created with a display name of OwaDownloadAttachments. If the request reports that the service principal already exists, continue to Step 2.

Step 2: Exclude it from the policy

  1. Click on View or Edit on the Conditional Access Policy you want to update.
  2. Under Target resources, select the Exclude tab.
  3. Choose Select resources, search for OwaDownloadAttachments, and select it.
  4. Save the policy.

Repeat Step 2 for each policy you want attachment operations exempted from.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft 365 Copilot: Use Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents in declarative agents
item.description:
[What and why]

Microsoft is introducing support for Microsoft Agent 365 agents that implement the Agent2Agent (A2A) protocol, allowing them to be used as connected agents in declarative agents built with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit.

This enhancement expands the types of external agent services that declarative agents can connect to. In addition to existing support for OpenAPI and Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, declarative agents can now connect to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling natural language interactions and support for more complex workflows.

This feature gives developers greater flexibility when building declarative agents while providing administrators centralized management and governance through the Microsoft 365 admin center.

[Rollout schedule]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Began in late August 2026 and expected to complete by late September 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft 365 administrators who manage agents in the Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Developers building declarative agents with Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Users who are assigned access to approved Microsoft Agent 365 agents

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft 365 Copilot
  • Microsoft 365 admin center
  • Microsoft 365 Agents Toolkit
  • Declarative agents

What will happen

  • Administrators can install Microsoft Agent 365 agents that support the Agent2Agent protocol from the All agents page in the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Declarative agents can use approved Agent2Agent-enabled agents as connected agents.
  • Agent2Agent support is added alongside existing support for OpenAPI and MCP server connections.
  • Users cannot install Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents themselves.
  • Administrators can review Agent2Agent-connected agents from the Connected agents tab in the declarative agent details page before approving their use.

[Action required and recommendations]

Action may be required.

Before rollout:

  • Review Microsoft Agent 365 agents available in the All agents page of the Microsoft 365 admin center.
  • Determine which Agent2Agent-enabled agents should be made available to users in your organization.
  • Review connected agents associated with declarative agents from the Connected agents tab before approving their use.
  • Update any internal governance, agent approval, or deployment processes as appropriate.

Consider notifying administrators and developers in your organization about the availability of Agent2Agent-connected agents and the associated review and approval process.

[Compliance considerations]

Compliance considerationAnswer
Does this change introduce or significantly modify AI, machine learning, or agent capabilities that interact with or provide access to customer data?Yes. This update introduces support for Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents as connected agents within declarative agents. Organizations should review how these connected agents interact with customer data before approving them for use.
Does this change provide end users with a new way to interact with generative AI?Yes. Users can interact with declarative agents that are connected to Agent2Agent-enabled agents, enabling new AI-powered experiences and workflows.
Does this change include an admin control?Yes. Administrators can install, review, and approve Agent2Agent-enabled Microsoft Agent 365 agents through the Microsoft 365 admin center before they are available for use.

item.title: [planForChange] (Updated) Migrate Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing before EWS deprecation
item.description:
Updated September 29, 2026: We have updated the content and timeline. Thank you for your patience.

[What and Why:]

Exchange Web Services (EWS) deprecation begins October 1, 2026. Cross-tenant collaboration features — Free/Busy, MailTips, and Calendar Sharing — currently rely on EWS.

Cross-tenant Free/Busy, MailTips will be available by September 2026 and Calendar Sharing will be available by mid-October 2026 via Microsoft 365 Cross-Tenant Access Policy, which replaces EWS-based cross-tenant collaboration.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • Worldwide: We will begin rolling out in August 2026 and expect to complete by September 15, 2026 for Free/Busy, Mailtips and October 15, 2026 for Calendar Sharing.
  • GCC: We will begin rolling out early September 2026 (previously mid-August) and expect to complete by September 30, 2026 (previously mid-September).
  • GCC High: We will begin rolling out early September 2026 and expect to complete by September 30, 2026.
  • DoD: We will begin rolling out early September 2026 and expect to complete by October 30, 2026 (previously end of September).

[Impact on your organization:]

Sharing Free/Busy, Calendars, and MailTips (e.g., out of office message) with another Microsoft 365 organization via Organization Relationship or Sharing Policy relies on Exchange Web Services (EWS), which is being deprecated. To preserve these cross-tenant collaboration scenarios, you will need to start migrating to Microsoft 365 Cross Tenant Access Policy.

Your tenant is affected if it uses any of the following Exchange Online configurations:

  • Organization Relationships — sharing Free/Busy or MailTips with other Microsoft 365 tenants 
  • Sharing Policies — sharing calendars externally, either via invitations sent to recipients in other Microsoft 365 organizations or calendars published for anonymous access via an internet URL

Run these commands in Exchange Online PowerShell to check if your tenant is affected: 

    • Get-OrganizationRelationship | Format-List Name, DomainNames, Enabled, FreeBusyAccessEnabled, FreeBusyAccessLevel, FreeBusyAccessScope, MailTipsAccessEnabled, MailTipsAccessLevel, MailTipsAccessScopeIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) either FreeBusyAccessEnabled: True or MailtipsAccessEnabled: True, and (3) the external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed. 
    • Get-SharingPolicy | Format-List Name, Domains, Enabled, DefaultIf results show (1) Enabled: True, and (2) the Domains property contains at least one rule with a CalendarSharingFreeBusy access level (Simple, Detail, or Reviewer), and (3) the targeted external organization is hosted in Microsoft 365, and (4) the policy is assigned to one or more mailboxes, your tenant is affected and in scope to migrate. Else, no action is needed.
    • Note: rules that begin with Anonymous: represent calendar publishing to anonymous internet recipients via a published URL - these also appear in this output.

What happens if I do nothing:

item.title: [stayInformed] (Updated) Updates to Tenant External Recipient Rate Limit (TERRL) Quotas for New, Trial, and Education Tenants
item.description:
Updated September 29, 2026: We have updated the timeline. Thank you for your patience. 

[What and Why:]

To strengthen protection against abuse and ensure fair use of Exchange Online resources, we are updating how the Tenant External Recipient Rate Limit (TERRL) quota is calculated for certain tenants.

These changes improve how quotas account for tenant age (how long the tenant has existed since creation), trial subscriptions, and educational organizations using free Education (EDU) licenses.

[Rollout Schedule:]

  • General Availability (Worldwide): Rolling out beginning mid-September 2026 and expected to complete by end of November 2026. 

[Impact on Your Organization:]

Who is affected:

  • Newly created tenants (first 60 days)
  • Trial tenants
  • Educational organizations with free EDU licenses

Platforms/Services:

  • Exchange Online
  • Exchange admin center (EAC)

What will happen:

TERRL quota calculations will change based on tenant status and licensing.

  • New tenant quotas (based on tenant age):
    • Less than 31 days: 10% of standard calculated quota
    • 31–60 days: 25% of standard calculated quota
    • More than 60 days: 100% of standard calculated quota
  • Trial tenants:
    • Daily TERRL quota reduced from 5,000 to 500 external recipients
  • Tenants with free EDU licenses (e.g. A1 licenses):
    • New formula applied: 500 × (Purchased Email Licenses^0.7 + Free EDU Licenses^0.3) + 9500
    • Free EDU licenses contribute to the quota at a lower weighting than purchased licenses
  • Tenants without free EDU licenses:
    • Existing formula remains unchanged: 500 × (Purchased Email Licenses^0.7) + 9500

If a tenant exceeds its quota:

  • Additional outbound messages to external recipients will be blocked until usage falls below the rolling 24-hour limit
  • Senders will receive one of the following Non-Delivery Reports (NDRs):
    • Trial tenants: 550 5.7.232 — Message blocked due to trial tenant external recipient limit
    • Non-trial tenants: 550 5.7.233 — Message blocked due to tenant external recipient limit

[Action Required / Recommendations:]

No immediate action is required.

Recommended actions:

  • Review the Tenant Outbound External Recipients Rate report in the Exchange admin center: EAC > Reports > Mail flow > Tenant Outbound External Recipients Rate.
  • Monitor:
    • Current TERRL quota
    • Outbound recipient volume
    • Percentage of quota consumed
    • Blocked recipients (if any)
    • TERRL enforcement status
  • If your organization regularly operates near or above quota consider migrating high-volume, application-driven outbound email to a third-party bulk email service or purchasing more licenses to cover your volume needs.

Learn more: Introducing Exchange Online Tenant Outbound Email Limits

[Compliance considerations:]

No compliance considerations identified, review as appropriate for your organization.

item.title: [stayInformed] Microsoft Teams: Enable Teams apps and agents for existing applications in your organization
item.description:

Organizations often use third-party applications such as ServiceNow, Workday, Jira, and others, but the corresponding Microsoft Teams apps and agents may not be enabled for users. As a result, users may switch between Teams and other applications even when an integrated Teams experience is available.

With this feature, admins can discover Teams apps and agents that correspond to applications already being used in their organization. Recommendations are prioritized using usage signals, helping admins identify opportunities to make those Teams experiences available to users already using the application, specific users and groups, or the entire organization. This helps bring existing business applications into the flow of work in Teams, reducing context switching and helping organizations realize more value from their software investments.

[Rollout schedule]

  • Targeted Release: Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026
  • General Availability (Worldwide, GCC): Beginning in early November 2026 and expected to complete by mid-November 2026

[Impact on your organization]

Who is affected

  • Microsoft Teams administrators managing app and agent deployment
  • Organizations using supported third-party applications that have corresponding Teams apps or agents

Platforms and services

  • Microsoft Teams
  • Teams admin center
  • Teams apps
  • Teams agents

What will happen

  • Admins will see recommendations in the Teams admin center for Teams apps and agents associated with applications already being used in their organization:

  • Recommendations will include usage signals to help admins identify where a Teams app or agent may provide the greatest value.
  • Admins can choose to make a recommended app or agent available to users already using the corresponding application, specific users and groups, or everyone in the organization.
  • Admins can choose to install the app or agent for applicable users.
  • No Teams apps or agents will be enabled automatically.
  • Existing app availability and installation settings will not change unless an administrator takes action.
  • Users may gain access to applications they already use directly within Teams, reducing the need to switch between applications.

[Action required and recommendations]

No action is required unless you want to use this feature.

  • Review this feature before rollout and determine whether you want to enable it in the Teams admin center.
  • If enabled, Microsoft will use signals indicating that users have signed in to applications within your organization to identify relevant Teams apps and agents and provide recommendations.
  • Review recommendations in the Teams admin center and determine which apps or agents should be made available or installed for users.
  • Communicate the change to Teams administrators responsible for app governance and deployment.
  • Update any internal documentation related to Teams app management, if applicable.

[Compliance considerations]
